Definition: properly, to swell up, i.e. figuratively (by implication of insolence) to devastate
BiblicalUsage: Shud means to devastate, to waste, and it appears once, in the psalm of protection: the destruction that wasteth at noonday. The pestilence walks in darkness, and this wasting walks at noon, in broad daylight, and the psalmist says it shall not come near the one who dwells in the secret place.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe destruction does not keep office hours, wasting at noonday as well as at midnight, and the only shelter is the secret place of the Most High.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
